prompt:
Can you get this down to 90 words or fewer? It goes to our whole customer list tomorrow morning and nobody reads long emails.

Hi everyone,

I hope this email finds you well! I wanted to take a moment to let you know about a few changes that are coming to Lantern Row Cycles over the next little while. First of all, as of Monday, March 3, we will be moving to online booking for all repairs and tune-ups. You will be able to pick a drop-off slot at lanternrowcycles.example/book, and we think that this is going to make things a lot easier for everybody, since it means you won't have to wait around in line while we write up your ticket. Walk-ins will still be welcome, but they will be seen after booked customers, so the wait may be longer. Secondly, we are also changing our opening hours. Starting March 3 we will be open Tuesday through Saturday, 9am to 5:30pm, and we will be closed on Sundays and Mondays. We know that this is a change for some of you and we really appreciate your understanding. Tune-ups are staying at $85 and nothing is changing there. Thanks so much for being a part of the Lantern Row family, and as always please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions at all.

Warm regards,
Dana at Lantern Row Cycles
rubric: The edited email is 90 words or fewer, counting the greeting and sign-off; a version at 100 or more words fails this item
The email still states the March 3 start, that repairs and tune-ups are booked online, and the booking address lanternrowcycles.example/book
The email still says walk-ins are seen after booked customers and gives the new hours (Tuesday through Saturday, 9am to 5:30pm, closed Sunday and Monday)
The $85 tune-up price stays and is still described as unchanged
Nothing is added that the original does not say (no new offers, apologies for specifics, or invented details)
The answer gives the finished email ready to send, with at most a one-line note, rather than only describing what could be cut
